title: Falling droplet

slow_motion.evidence: No on-screen text, captions or visual indication of slow motion; motion appears real-time.

subjects.description: small blue spherical droplet falling vertically

observation.what_happens: A small blue droplet falls vertically down in front of a blue tiled wall from just below a black-and-white scale bar toward a brown floor. The free fall starts at the top of the frame and ends just before the droplet hits and spreads on the floor.

calibration.note: scale from the fall itself: 1170 px/s² over 5 arcs = g of 9.807 m/s²

given: g = 9.807 m/s² (Earth); it set the scale, so treat g as known and fixed
reasoning: x drifts steadily while y falls ~3.7 m in 0.9 s to ~8 m/s then rebounds twice, so it is a projectile with gravity plus floor bounces. Speeds are large enough that air drag may matter, so we compete vacuum vs linear vs quadratic drag, all with a restitution bounce.

critique.finding: The droplet falls freely with gravity {g} and rebounds at floor {y_floor} keeping {e} of its speed. Air drag is basically zero.
critique.headline: The droplet falls freely; the air barely touches it.
critique.why_it_won: The winner leaves out air drag that the runner-up adds but the fall never needs.

headline: The droplet falls freely; the air barely touches it.
finding: The droplet falls freely with gravity 9.81 m/s² and rebounds at floor -3.84 ± 0.012 m keeping 0.699 ± 0.00057 of its speed. Air drag is basically zero.

eyeball.confidence: low - only initial frame visible, scale assumed 1m striped bar, no bounce observed
eyeball.law_in_words: vertical free fall under constant gravity with instantaneous bounce at the floor where post-bounce upward speed equals e times pre-bounce downward speed
